details: On September 2nd, a sharp escalation in tensions between the US and Iran, involving US strikes and Iranian retaliation, led to a flash crash in the cryptocurrency market. Bitcoin temporarily fell below $78,000, and other major cryptocurrencies experienced significant declines due to a global safe-haven sell-off and liquidity panic. The conflict continues to be monitored for its potential to impact energy markets and global financial stability.
title: US-Iran Conflict Escalation Causes Crypto Market Drop

details: Bitcoin's price, after reclaiming $81,000 due to easing concerns about Federal Reserve interest rate hikes on September 4th, fell below $80,000 on September 5th. This dip followed a stronger-than-expected US jobs report for August, which showed nonfarm payrolls increasing by 162,000—more than triple economists' forecasts. The robust jobs data has led to market uncertainty regarding the Fed's future monetary policy decisions.
title: Bitcoin Dips Below $80K After Strong US Jobs Data

details: On September 2nd, G20 finance ministers and central bank governors convened and agreed to work towards improving the clarity of regulatory and supervisory frameworks for digital assets. They acknowledged the benefits of digital financial innovation for inclusive growth and committed to supporting responsible and balanced regulation to preserve financial stability, promote growth, and enable sound innovation.
title: G20 Pledges Clearer Rules for Digital Assets and Stablecoins

details: Fidelity International's 2026 outlook, reported on September 4th, highlights Bitcoin's evolution from a speculative asset to a significant macro hedge. This shift is occurring amidst escalating geopolitical tensions and concerns over currency debasement. The report notes accelerating institutional adoption, with corporate treasuries, sovereign wealth funds, and private banks increasingly engaging with Bitcoin.
title: Fidelity: Bitcoin Emerging as Macro Hedge Amid Geopolitical Risks
